title: Prime Factor Trees
summary: One lesson for a weak group after LCM and HCF: split a number into two with a factor tree, circling each prime until every branch ends in a prime, write the primes as a product, then write that product in index form. Harry draws the trees; the deck holds the questions and the answers. No calculators.

els.text: Split. Circle the primes. Write the product.
Write a number as a product of its prime factors using a factor tree, and give the answer in index form.

•  Split a number into two numbers and circle every prime
•  Write the primes as a product, smallest first
•  Write a product of primes in index form, such as $2^2 \times 3$
A number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that divides exactly into another number.
The answer to a multiplication. $2 \times 3 = 6$, so 6 is the product.
The small raised number (also called a power). It counts how many times a number is multiplied by itself: the 3 in $2^3$.

A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

The primes up to 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

1 is not a prime number.
Say prime or not prime. If not, name two numbers that multiply to it.

explanation: $21 = 3 \times 7$, so it has more than two factors.
$26 = 2 \times 13$, so it has more than two factors.
$38 = 2 \times 19$, so it has more than two factors.
$39 = 3 \times 13$, so it has more than two factors.

els.text: Even: 2 goes in  ·  Ends in 0 or 5: 5 goes in  ·  Digits add to a 3 table number: 3 goes in

explanation: It ends in 5, so 5 goes in. It is odd, and the digits add to 11, so neither 2 nor 3 does.
It is even, so 2 goes in. The digits add to 7, which is not in the 3 times table, and it does not end in 0 or 5.
The digits add to 6, which is in the 3 times table, so 3 goes in. It is odd and does not end in 0 or 5.
It is even, so 2 goes in. The digits add to 15, which is in the 3 times table, so 3 goes in too.

slides.title: Write the primes as a product

els.text: Write the primes as a product
Read off the circled primes. Write them smallest first.
A product is what you get when you multiply.
Multiply the primes. Do you get the number?
Draw a tree for 18. Count each prime.

Index form is a short way to write the same prime multiplied again and again.

$3 \times 3 = 3^2$

The small raised number, the index, counts how many times the prime is written.

slides.title: What does the small number mean?

els.text: What does the small number mean?
It counts the repeats. It does not multiply.

items.title: Who is right about $5^{3}$?
question: Who is right?
answer: Leo is right: $5^{3}$ means three 5s multiplied together, $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.
explanation: The small 3 says the 5 is written three times.

options.reasoning: Multiplies the 5 by the index: $5 \times 3 = 15$. The index counts the 5s.
$5 \times 3 = 15$ is not $125$: the index is a count, not a times.

misconception.label: Reads the index as a multiplier instead of a count of repeats

els.text:
•  Split a number into two numbers bigger than 1. Circle a prime when you reach one.
•  Keep splitting until every branch ends in a circled prime.
•  Write the primes as a product, smallest first.
•  Index form counts the repeats: $2 \times 2 \times 3 = 2^2 \times 3$.
